programme: YY1 acting upstream of TFEB, the master transcriptional regulator of the autophagy-lysosomal (CLEAR) network: YY1 controls TFEB expression/activity and TFEB in turn drives lysosomal biogenesis and autophagic clearance.
role_in_a: In Alzheimer's disease, YY1-driven TFEB activity restores microglial/neuronal autophagic-lysosomal flux to clear amyloid and other aggregates, and YY1 separately controls TREM2, a microglial clearance receptor; boosting this axis (e.g. via TFEB activation) is reported to mitigate pathology.
role_in_b: In glioblastoma, TFEB governs autophagy as a stress-response/survival node under genotoxic stress and reprograms tumor-associated macrophages toward a less immunosuppressive state, while YY1 sits upstream of progression and drug-resistance pathways (e.g. the DLD-EphA2 axis, BLACAT1/miR-605-3p) that are proposed to converge on the same autophagy machinery.
shared_axis: Both diseases occur in brain parenchyma where proteostasis stress and myeloid cell (microglia/macrophage) plasticity are central: TFEB's autophagy-lysosomal programme, gated by YY1, is a convergent node that determines whether stressed neurons/microglia in AD and stressed tumor cells/macrophages in GBM survive, clear material, or resist further insult, giving two very different brain diseases a shared molecular lever even without a documented clinical link between them.
reasoning: Both YY1 and TFEB are independently documented with multiple, specific (non-review) papers in each disease, and one AD paper explicitly names a YY1-TFEB pathway, giving the module internal coherence beyond co-occurrence in the network. No retrieved paper states that AD and GBM share this axis together, so the connection is inferred from each disease's separate literature rather than a stated fact, which caps the verdict at 'supported' rather than 'established'.
support: PMID 40832968 (YY1-TFEB pathway enhances autophagy in AD, direct mechanistic link between the two carrying factors); PMID 37044212 (YY1 regulates TREM2, protective in AD); PMID 40768913 (YY1 gene interactions in AD, computational); PMID 42636682 (TFEB restores microglial phagocytic-lysosomal balance in AD model); PMID 41664344 (TFEB pathway component alleviates AD progression); PMID 41506439 (TFEB-mediated endocytosis mitigates amyloid pathology); PMID 41803045 (YY1 upregulates DLD to drive glioblastoma progression); PMID 40595024 (YY1/lncRNA BLACAT1/miR-605-3p axis in glioblastoma); PMID 40867514 (YY1 as central node in glioblastoma drug resistance); PMID 42214785 (TFEB activation reprograms immunosuppressive macrophages in glioblastoma); PMID 41248831 (TFEB inhibition under genotoxic stress promotes glioblastoma apoptosis).
how_to_falsify: Knock down YY1 in an AD microglial model and a glioblastoma cell/macrophage co-culture in parallel; measure TFEB nuclear localization/target-gene induction (e.g. CLEAR-network reporter) and downstream phenotypes (amyloid clearance vs. tumor cell autophagic survival/macrophage polarization). If YY1 loss fails to reduce TFEB activity in glioblastoma cells the way it does in the AD model — i.e., the YY1-TFEB link demonstrated in AD does not replicate in glioblastoma — the shared-axis claim is falsified.
caveats: Both diseases share tissue (brain) but not cell type of origin — AD acts through neurons/microglia, GBM through glioma cells and tumor-associated macrophages — so 'shared axis' means a shared regulatory lever in overlapping cell populations, not a shared disease process. Support (34/64 patient-group comparisons, ~53%) is the highest among all listed factors but still leaves roughly half of comparisons discordant, and only 6 independent cohort pairs underlie the 64 comparisons, so replication is limited. YY1 ReMap binding evidence is thin (1 of 25 targets bound) and TFEB has none, so the module rests on transcript-level/mRNA regulatory inference rather than confirmed direct binding. Excluding KLF1 (erythroid programme, glioblastoma-only evidence), NRG1 (RTK/growth-factor programme, separately supported but no literature tying it to YY1/TFEB), and CRX/SIM1/ZHX2/ZHX3/ELF5/IKZF4/MKX/ZBTB32 (no disease evidence, several tissue-mismatched like photoreceptor-specific CRX) keeps the account from overreaching into factors that recur in the network but aren't documented players. The tissue-generic exclusion list (SOX10, NOTCH1, ZEB1, NR3C1, TAL1, RFX5, STAT4, EGR4, HDAC7) removes the 'obvious' glial/immune master regulators, confirming YY1-TFEB is not simply a generic brain signature being relabeled as disease-specific.
